newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ARGENTINA'S MENOTTI TIPPED FOR SAMPDORIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA'S MENOTTI TIPPED FOR SAMPDORIA.

text.p: Argentina's former World Cup-winning coach Cesar Luis Menotti could be at Sampdoria next season while Napoli have chosen Piacenza's Bortolo Mutti as their new boss, Italian newspapers said on Saturday.
"Menotti, all that is lacking is Sampdoria's announcement," said the daily Tuttosport in a headline.

The Gazzetta dello Sport said the 59-year-old chain-smoking Independiente coach, who has spent time in Spain with Barcelona and Atletico Madrid, was increasingly mentioned as the man most likely to replace Sweden's Sven-Goran Eriksson.

Eriksson, who accepted and then turned down a hefty offer from English club Blackburn Rovers, has said he is leaving Sampdoria and is assumed to be joining Lazio although neither he nor the Rome club has confirmed the move.
Tuttosport said Menotti, who helped Argentina to win the 1978 World Cup, met team officials and members of the Mantovani family who run Sampdoria over Easter in Buenos Aires.
Napoli coach Luigi Simone has already announced he will be leaving the southern club at the end of the season and is expected to take over at Inter Milan.
Inter coach Roy Hodgson took the job at Blackburn after Eriksson had backed out of it.
The Gazzetta said financially-strapped Napoli had chosen Mutti over Udinese coach Alberto Zaccheroni, Ravenna's Walter Novellino and Torino's Mauro Sandreani.
